headline: GOLD POSTS BEST WEEK IN 2 MONTHS — $250 RALLY FROM $3,869 FLOOR, CENTRAL BANK BUYING HITS 2026 HIGH
snippet: Gold logged its best weekly performance in over two months, surging approximately $250 or 5% from an October 30 low of $3,869.85 to a Thursday high of $4,121 — driven by mid-week Dollar weakness, the Bank of England's surprise rate hike, and reportedly the highest pace of central bank gold buying in 2026 — before Friday's stronger-than-expected October payrolls report cut the metal back to approximately $4,047. Silver held the $52 level and closed the week positively despite Friday's macro headwind, with the gold-silver ratio compressing to 78.3. The weekly gain was the largest since early August and sets up a contested macro picture heading into next week: Barrick Mining's Q3 results on Monday, November 9, and China's critical minerals export control decision on November 10 are the two catalysts the market is watching.

headline: BARRICK REPORTS Q3 MONDAY: ZACKS PROJECTS 22.5% REVENUE JUMP TO $5.1B AT $4,000+ GOLD
snippet: Barrick Mining Corporation (NYSE: GOLD / TSX: ABX) reports Q3 2026 results before the bell on Monday, November 9, with Zacks projecting consolidated revenue of approximately $5.08 billion — a 22.5% increase year-over-year. Barrick beat its Q2 guidance by producing 796,000 gold ounces and analysts expect continued production improvement in Q3 at spot gold prices well above $4,000. The November 9 release is the most closely watched earnings event in the gold equities calendar this month: Barrick's realized costs and free cash flow margins at current bullion prices will set the benchmark narrative for producer valuations across the entire gold equities complex, and the market reaction will likely determine whether gold equities begin closing their persistent discount to bullion.

headline: BANK OF ENGLAND SURPRISE HIKE SENDS GOLD TO $4,121 — SILVER LAGS AT $52.78 AS MONETARY POLICY DIVERGES
snippet: The Bank of England's unexpected November 5 rate hike briefly sent gold to $4,121 per ounce as the U.S. dollar weakened on global monetary policy divergence — before Thursday's data shifted focus back to U.S. inflation ahead of Friday's payrolls report. The BoE action follows the ECB's hold last month and contrasts with the Fed's hawkish dot-plot posture, creating the kind of multi-directional central bank environment that has historically supported gold as a neutral reserve asset. Silver lagged at $52.78 on the day, compressing the gold-silver ratio and prompting debate over whether gold's monetary premium is running ahead of silver's industrial demand story as year-end approaches.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR SNAPS UP NOBLE PLAINS URANIUM IN WYOMING ISR DEAL AT $98/LB LONG-TERM PRICE
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy announced a binding letter of intent to acquire all of Noble Plains Uranium in an all-stock transaction on November 4, adding Wyoming in-situ recovery (ISR) uranium projects to its existing Oregon Aurora asset at a time when Cameco's long-term uranium indicator reached US$98 per pound — the highest in the current cycle. Wyoming's established ISR regulatory framework and existing operator network make it among the most drill-to-production-ready uranium jurisdictions in North America, and the deal underscores how junior uranium consolidation is accelerating as utilities seek domestic supply security ahead of the next contracting wave. Spot uranium traded near US$91.55 per pound at the time of the announcement.

headline: ENERGY FUELS Q3: $29.2M REVENUE, $88.90/LB URANIUM REALIZED + WHITE MESA REE PROCESSING SCALES UP
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU / TSX: EFR) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $29.2 million on November 4, with a weighted-average realized uranium sale price of $88.90 per pound — a premium above spot reflecting the company's contracted book. The White Mesa Mill in Utah — the only operating conventional uranium mill in the United States — is expanding its rare earth element (REE) processing operations, positioning the asset as a dual critical minerals processor as Washington accelerates domestic REE supply incentives. In the same week, Uranium Energy Corp separately signed definitive long-term supply agreements with two U.S. nuclear utilities, underscoring a tightening long-term contracting environment that is driving realized prices for established producers well above the spot market.

headline: WESDOME Q3 GOLD OUTPUT FALLS 18% TO 41,287 OZ — EAGLE RIVER GRADES SLIDE; Q4 MUST CLOSE A 50K-OZ GAP
snippet: Wesdome Gold Mines (TSX: WDO) reported Q3 2026 gold production of 41,287 ounces — an 18% year-over-year decline — as lower-than-expected grades at its Eagle River mine in Ontario dragged performance below consensus. Year-to-date production stands at approximately 130,414 ounces, requiring roughly 50,000 ounces in Q4 to reach the low end of full-year guidance of 180,000–205,000 ounces. The company stated results will fall below the guidance midpoint while maintaining that Q4 is expected to be the year's strongest quarter, with capital investment programs at both Eagle River and the Kiena mine in Quebec supporting multi-year growth. Shares fell approximately 9% on the news — a sharp reminder that at $4,000+ gold, investors are demanding production delivery rather than growth narratives.

headline: LME COPPER CRATERS TO 3-MONTH LOW AT $13,775 AS AI SELLOFF BITES — CHINA PHYSICAL PREMIUM HITS RECORD $217/T
snippet: LME three-month copper dropped to $13,775 per tonne — a three-month low — on November 6 as renewed selling pressure in AI and technology stocks weighed on the metal most closely linked to the data center buildout narrative, with bears adding positions while bulls reduced exposure. The LME-COMEX copper premium briefly flipped to a discount overnight before recovering. The disconnect between paper and physical markets remains extreme: the Yangshan copper import premium — a real-time indicator of Chinese physical demand — held at a record $217.50 per tonne, suggesting downstream Chinese buyers are aggressively acquiring physical copper even as Western macro traders de-risk on AI sector volatility. The divergence between paper weakness and physical strength is the clearest argument copper bulls have that the LME decline overstates real demand destruction.

headline: LODESTAR METALS HITS ALL 4 TARGETS IN MAIDEN NEVADA DRILL — 71.6M AT 0.9 G/T GOLD EQ AT CROWN NORTH
snippet: Lodestar Metals (TSXV: LSTR) reported final assay results from its maiden 2,820-metre drill program at the Gold Run project in Nevada, hitting gold-silver mineralisation at all four tested targets — including 71.6 metres grading 0.9 g/t gold equivalent at Crown North and a higher-grade intercept of 16.8 metres at 6.1 g/t gold and 41.1 g/t silver at Robbers Knob. Discovering mineralisation across all four first-pass targets in a maiden program is an unusually strong validation of the geological model. Gold Run sits in a structurally active Nevada corridor with established infrastructure, and the multi-target results support a larger resource-definition drill program heading into 2027.

headline: RADISSON MINING EXTENDS HIGH-GRADE GOLD BELOW HISTORIC O'BRIEN MINE IN QUÉBEC ABITIBI
snippet: Radisson Mining (TSXV: RDS) announced drill results extending high-grade gold mineralization both below and adjacent to the former O'Brien gold mine in the Abitibi region of Québec — one of Canada's most productive gold districts. Nine holes representing wedge branches from three pilot holes targeted deep high-grade gold below historic workings, aiming to demonstrate that the O'Brien system extends at depth with grades comparable to the mine's historic production record. Drilling wedge branches from existing pilot holes maximizes efficiency in deep targeting, minimizes cost, and allows rapid footprint expansion. The O'Brien system sits on the prolific Cadillac-Larder Lake break, the structural corridor hosting several of Canada's most significant gold deposits.

headline: GOLD'S $250 WEEKLY SURGE FACES THE NOVEMBER GAUNTLET — BARRICK, CHINA REE DECISION, FED ALL DUE NEXT WEEK
snippet: Mitrade's post-payrolls analysis of gold's $250 weekly rally identifies the November 10 expiry of China's rare earth export control pause and Barrick Mining's November 9 Q3 results as the two binary events that will test whether gold can sustain its best weekly gain in over two months. October payrolls came in stronger than expected at approximately 189,000, reviving December Fed rate hike speculation and knocking gold from $4,121 to $4,047 — but the weekly base is high enough that even a modest pullback next week would still constitute a bullish technical structure. The analysis argues that $4,000 now functions as the new structural support, that central bank buying provides a demand floor Western retail investors often underestimate, and that the November-December seasonal window historically adds 3–5% to gold prices in sustained bull markets.

headline: 5 CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH IN NOVEMBER 2026 — AGNICO, BARRICK, KINROSS, IAMGOLD, ALAMOS PROFILED
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's November 2026 equity preview flags Agnico Eagle, Barrick, Kinross, IAMGOLD, and Alamos Gold as the five TSX-listed gold miners best positioned to capture upside at $4,000+ gold — while warning that investors' primary question for each is production volume delivery versus cost creep at current energy and labour rates. The analysis notes the persistent discount of gold equities to physical bullion as either a value opportunity or a signal that the market sees structural margin compression at current output levels. The piece argues Agnico Eagle's track record of guidance delivery makes it the clearest buy among TSX majors, while Alamos represents the most compelling junior-to-mid-cap growth story at current valuations given its Mulatos and Island Gold growth profile.

headline: 2 RARE EARTH STOCKS TO BUY BEFORE NOVEMBER 10 — AND THE ONE TO SELL AS CHINA'S DECISION LOOMS
snippet: A Yahoo Finance rare earth stock analysis frames USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) as the two domestic rare earth names to hold through the November 10 binary event — when China's rare earth export control pause expires and Beijing either reinstates restrictions (bullish for Western producers) or extends the moratorium. The article identifies one rare earth name as a sell, citing either concentration risk in a single Chinese-dependent processing step or valuation stretched beyond near-term cash flow. MP Materials confirmed saleable magnet deliveries to General Motors starting in Q4 2026, while USAR's Blacksburg, South Carolina manufacturing complex — a $1.2 billion facility targeting 6,400 metric tonnes of NdFeB magnets annually — broke ground in September and validates the demand narrative regardless of Beijing's near-term decision.
